Internal leakage is defined as leakage within the cavity of a component, and external leakage is defined as leakage from a component or fitting to the external environment surrounding the pipeline. The main reasons for hydraulic cylinder leakage are: first, the mating surfaces of mating parts have gaps at the joint surfaces; second, there is a pressure difference (pressure drop) across the sealing surfaces, which affects the efficiency of the hydraulic cylinder, the speed and rate of cylinder advancement, and/or output force, etc. It also causes the hydraulic working medium to further heat up, which may lead to safety accidents; external leakage causes environmental pollution, causes work stoppages, and may cause fire hazards, etc. Therefore, whether it is leakage or external leakage, it may be a serious problem that must be taken seriously. Internal leakage (clearance) and external leakage (clearance) are mandatory inspection items for hydraulic cylinder factory testing, with specific reference to JB/T 10205-2010 and GB/T 15622-2005 standards. Hydraulic cylinder leakage is mainly collar (penetration, string) leakage.

Being able to prevent or reduce leakage of equipment is generally referred to as sealing or sealing devices. Sealing devices are composed of one or more sealing components and related structural components (such as grooves, metal rings, etc.) combined to form the assembly. Sealing devices commonly used to prevent leakage and/or prevent contaminants from entering components include: guides (supports), wipers, dust seals (Y-type, V-type supports), and anti-fouling seals collectively referred to as sealing components (some are called MT/T seals). The function of sealing is to seal the joint surfaces of two coupled surfaces, cut off the leakage channel or increase the leakage channel resistance. The main performance indicators measuring the sealing effect of a seal are: leakage rate (leakage amount/time or leakage amount/distance), applicable friction and wear characteristics, service life and applicable working conditions (pressure, speed, temperature, etc.). Currently, in China, the hydraulic seal design standards and levels, as well as processing technology and equipment, seal component structural types and parameters, sealing materials (rubber and plastic materials), additives and testing, etc. all have made relatively great progress. The sealing performance of hydraulic cylinders also has relatively great improvement. In summary, hydraulic cylinder pressure, speed, temperature, product quality improvements, service life extension, and reliability and other technical performance can to a large extent depend on the hydraulic cylinder sealing device (system) and its design.

The above-mentioned sealing is to prevent or reduce leakage measures (actions or methods). This is a concept that also means "sealing" is called "leakage seal." In addition, there are representations of leakage of this kind of phenomenon or state, which is the opposite of another concept called "leakage seal."

2. Classification of Seals

Seals are divided into static seals and dynamic seals. Static seals are for sealing components (assemblies, fittings) that have no relative motion; dynamic seals are for sealing components (assemblies, fittings) that have relative motion. This type of seal is in a relatively static working state. For the requirements of static seals, dynamic seals must not only ensure sealing force in addition to withstanding the operating pressure, but must also consider the friction, wear, and heat generated by relative movement of the contact area; ensuring a certain level of sealing performance while also ensuring that the movement performance meets the requirements, but because of the requirements for movement components' support and orientation, according to whether the sealed coupling surface is sliding or rotating motion, dynamic seals are further divided into dynamic seals and rotary seals. Dynamic seals in hydraulic cylinders include the piston (and its related) rod, piston, guide sleeve and piston rod direction seal combinations. According to the contact relationship between dynamic seals and mating seal surfaces, reciprocating seals can also be divided into contact seals and non-contact seals. Reciprocating motion dynamic seals can be further called piston seals (or called piston, rod seals) and piston rod seals (or called shaft seals, inner diameter seals). Static seals can be divided into flat static seals (end face seals) and cylindrical static seals (radial seals, inner and outer diameter static seals). sections.text: This is because: 1) Single-lip rubber dust seal rings only have dust-proof function, but do not have auxiliary seal function. 2) Even using double-lip rubber dust seal rings, achieving "zero" leakage is also very difficult. 3) Even under certain specific conditions where the external leakage of the hydraulic cylinder is "zero," once the working conditions change (such as oil temperature rising), external leakage may still occur, and the only question is how much the leakage amount is.

For this reason, as long as there is a dust-proof seal ring in front of the "leakage oil," through leakage passage introduction or open-type discharge or other open methods, the seal will always maintain "zero" pressure on the outside, and the seal performance can be maintained for a long time, the piston rod external leakage process under reduced conditions becomes as small or achieves "zero."
If the dust seal ring in front of the leakage is blocked, the commonly used method is to use a double-lip nitrile rubber seal ring.

What needs to be explained here is: (1) In GB/T 32217-2016 test display schematic diagram, the "leakage measurement port" is set to measure the position of its hydraulic cylinder leakage passage, and it should have reference and specified values. The specified "leakage collection area" (for piston rod with diameter d ≥ 36mm, length of 20mm ± 5mm) is also very important. (2) Currently, many products have the leakage channel set at the second seal ring of the piston rod seal system, and this approach is incorrect.
4. Selection of Single and Double Dust Seal Ring Issues
The dust seal ring is an important component of the piston rod seal system, and it should be given due attention.

In GB/T 10708.3-2000 (reciprocating motion rubber seal ring structural dimensions series, Part 3: rubber dust seal ring), three basic forms of dust seals are specified. Among these, one type is a double-lip dust seal ring.

In the piston rod seal system, when you want to achieve "zero" piston rod leakage, it is not whether a single-lip or double-lip is used that matters, but rather whether a single-lip dust seal ring is sufficient as long as one leakage collection is done.
In coaxial seal systems with piston rod dust-proof seals, regardless of whether the coaxial sealing components have a "rod return" function, double-lip dust seals are used.
For stepped-form sealing components (stepped-form sealing and dust-proof combined), in the piston rod seal system, generally single-lip dust seals are used.

Single-lip dust rings and double-lip dust rings have been collectively called single-use dust rings. Dust rings in the cylinder travel during the process (referred to as the rod section) can also have the function of removing surface dirt and pollutants, such as mud, dust, and moisture (water); and another function of the double-use ring is to remove (exclude) all remaining oil film of the seal component between the seal surfaces, this is a double-use dust seal component. But regardless of whether single-use or double-use, as per GB/T 10708.3-2000, if pressure applied is at the pressure value, it may still be possible to leak.

Dust-proof seals — even without applied pressure or rated constant pressure conditions, mainly are non-pressure seals, that is to say there are mainly non-pressure dust seals, because they do not have oil-sealing function.

Commonly used lip-type rubber dust rings and polyurethane rubber dust rings need to be replaced regularly. Floating or submerged ring-type dust ring materials may also be made of glass fiber reinforced nylon or similar materials. Regarding abrasion requirements, they are not strictly required, reducing the wear rate and extending service life, especially for piston rod seal reciprocating motion, when the dust seal ring wears during the stroke.
2.10.8 Preliminary Determination of Hydraulic Cylinder Seal Working Conditions

Hydraulic cylinder seals refer to the seals that enable the hydraulic cylinder's sealing function to work properly in a unidirectional manner. The hydraulic cylinder also has various functional sealing requirements. Among these, the sealing working condition is to ensure the hydraulic cylinder seal has a relatively long service life.
